method: The open string's frequency comes from scientific pitch notation with A4 fixed at 440 Hz: f = 440 x 2^((MIDI - 69) / 12), where MIDI = (octave + 1) x 12 + semitones above C. Harmonic n sounds at n times that frequency and has n - 1 nodes, each at k/n of the vibrating length for k = 1 to n - 1, so the node nearest the nut sits at 1/n of the scale length and its distances from nut and bridge are L x k/n and L x (1 - k/n). The interval above the open string is 12 x log2(n) semitones; the nearest equal-tempered note is that interval added to the open string's MIDI number and rounded, and the deviation in cents is 100 x the fractional semitone left over, so harmonic 2 lands on an exact octave, harmonic 5 is about 13.7 cents flatter than an equal-tempered major third and harmonic 7 about 31.2 cents flatter than a minor seventh. The scale length is limited to 8-40 inches, the octave to 0-8 and the harmonic to a whole number from 2 to 16; text, out-of-range values, a fractional harmonic and an unknown note name are rejected with an actionable message. Nodes are positions on a string at rest: fretting, bending, saddle compensation and string stiffness move a real node slightly. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Harmonic series on a stretched string: the n-th harmonic sounds at n times the fundamental frequency and has nodes at k/n of the vibrating length
Equal temperament with A4 = 440 Hz: the interval of harmonic n is 12 x log2(n) semitones, and cents are 100 x the leftover fraction after rounding to the nearest note
